payload.props_realized:
The frame records TWO value props, not eight. My write_stories fill labelled eight CAPABILITIES (P1-P8, lifted from the pitch) as props; that was a mislabelling, corrected here, and it is why the mapping below is against the frame's register rather than against the story fill's own headings.

PROP 1 — THE AGENT WALKING THE LOOP. Realized by S2 (the agent who stops writing scripts), S3 (the second agent), S4 (the wrong argument). Its need register N1-N5:
  N1 read any source the process mandates — S2 slides 1-3.
  N2 find things without four attempts, WITH CONTEXT — S2 slide 3, and the corrected pass line is what that slide is written against.
  N3 know the rules that bind this step — NO STORY. Gap.
  N4 edit many sites at once — S2 slide 4.
  N5 search what shipped — S2 slide 3 (the ref-scoped search).

PROP 2 — THE OWNER WHO OWNS AN ITERATION THEY DID NOT WATCH. Realized by S1 (the gate that reviews itself), S5 (the check that does not pretend), S6 (the reader six months out), S7 (the owner reading chat). Its need register N6-N12:
  N6 mechanical checks are mechanical — S5 slides 1-2.
  N7 a lint never parks an unattended run — S5 slide 3 (defer, with the reason).
  N8 the record survives carelessness — NO STORY. Gap.
  N9 the audit distinguishes computed from asserted — NO STORY. S5 is adjacent but never shows the owner distinguishing the two, which is the whole of the need.
  N10 a gate is reviewed, not just filled — S1, and this gate is itself the instance.
  N11 a reopen verdict does something — S1 slide 4, S6.
  N12 the red-team round is adversarial, not decorative — S1 slide 3.

So: both props are realized, which is what this field literally asks. But three needs — N3, N8, N9 — have no story at all, and that is the finding that drives the verdict.

Separately and in the other direction: S3 (engine promotion), S4 (refusals over confident wrong answers) and S7 (the owner reading chat) realize PROP 1 and PROP 2 but correspond to NO numbered need. That is not a violation — the need lists are not claimed exhaustive — but it is a stale register: all three came from owner instructions issued AFTER the frame was written. Recorded, and M3 sources those requirements to the stories and the owner rulings directly.
payload.stories_generalized:
Every story sits inside a use case, and every use case traces back:
  S1 → UC-A (close a gate under review), main scenario steps 1-7.
  S2 → UC-B (find a fact wherever it lives) for slides 1-3, UC-C (change many places at once) for slide 4. One story spanning two use cases, because it is one working session crossing two user goals.
  S3 → UC-D (give the running lane an engine change).
  S4 → UC-E (call a tool wrongly).
  S5 → UC-F (check what can be checked).
  S6 → UC-A extension 6a, where the reopen is carried out and the prior fills survive as superseded.
  S7 → UC-G (report to someone who is away).
No use case exists without a story behind it. Every extension is numbered off the step it interrupts, and no step names a UI mechanism — checked by reading the seven scenarios for tool names and finding none: they say 'the machine refuses', not 'se_loop_submit returns SE-C-030'.
payload.roles_covered:
Six roles mapped at map_stakeholders, each appearing in at least one use case as actor or stakeholder:
  THE OWNER — UC-G primary stakeholder; UC-A stakeholder interest; UC-A ext 6b.
  THE WALKING AGENT — primary actor in UC-B, UC-C, UC-D, UC-E, UC-G.
  THE PARALLEL AGENT — UC-D's named stakeholder, and the reason for its extensions 2a and 4b.
  THE REVIEWING AGENT — primary actor in UC-A. Kept distinct from the walking agent deliberately.
  THE FUTURE READER — UC-A stakeholder; served by ext 6a and UC-B's ref search.
  THE ENGINE AS SHARED JUDGE — not a person, and named anyway: UC-D exists entirely to protect it.
Six tensions named with reasoning, none left as 'none found': T1 walking vs reviewing agent (the iteration's core, with the author's own failure as evidence); T2 walking vs parallel agent (resolved by promotion, with its cost stated); T3 owner vs agent over precision (resolved by expanding identifiers); T4 engine-as-judge vs its builder (declared, not resolved — hence the workaround-then-record law); T5 future reader vs walking agent over rewrites (resolved by superseding rather than deleting); T6 owner vs engine over dependencies (resolved by the owner's own reversal).
payload.excluded_stated:
Yes, at draw_context, binding and system-level: no authoring of method CONTENT; no board, browser or phone work; no turning items into ledger nodes; no general-purpose agent shell; no retiring v1; no second mechanism for one job EXCEPT where the jobs are genuinely two; and no answering a tooling gap by keeping the human in the loop. Each is sharper than M1's vision-level non-goals, and each names why it is out rather than merely that it is.
One of them is load-bearing for this gate: 'does NOT turn items into ledger nodes' is what makes N9's mechanical half honestly deferrable rather than a false pass.
payload.examples_formulated:
The formulated examples are the numbered scenario steps and their extensions in the seven use cases, plus the slides they generalize. These are the examples' BIRTH per meth-examples-checkable — roles now, nodes later.
The ones that must become checkable at validation, named so they are not quietly dropped:
  UC-A step 2 and ext 2a — a gate form carries all four rounds as REQUIRED, and a blank round is refused. Mechanically checkable across every gate in the machine.
  UC-A ext 6a — reopen re-activates the cone AND leaves the prior evidence readable. Checkable by reading a superseded file after a reopen; already exercised in this very gate, where the first-pass frame was read to recover N1-N9.
  UC-B step 3 — a match carries context in the SAME call. The pass line names one call.
  UC-C ext 2a — one bad edit in a batch writes nothing.
  UC-D ext 4b and 4c — a red suite promotes nothing and NAMES the failures; a suite that runs nothing counts as red.
  UC-E ext 2a — absent and explicitly-null are different.
  UC-F ext 2a — an uncomputable check defers with its reason and never passes.
Evidence sides stay empty until validation, as the method requires.
payload.verify_round:
BUILT IT RIGHT. Four input states since the last gate, each opened rather than trusted.

1. draw_context — read. Claim: boundary, neighbours with interfaces, binding excluded list. Verified: inside/outside/neighbours all present, five neighbours each named WITH what crosses them. HOLDS. One thing I checked specifically because it is easy to fake: the excluded list is binding and reasoned, not a list of things nobody was going to do anyway — 'does NOT author method content' and 'does NOT keep the human in the loop as the fix' both rule OUT things I was actively tempted by today.

2. map_stakeholders — read. Claim: six roles, six tensions with reasoning. Verified against the use cases: every role appears as actor or stakeholder somewhere. HOLDS.

3. write_stories — read against its OWN claim, and it FAILED that reading. It claims each slideshow 'realizes a named value prop' and then names eight props that do not exist in the frame. The frame records two props with needs N1-N12; the story fill invented P1-P8 from the pitch's feature list. This is exactly the failure the verify round exists to catch: a claim that describes itself accurately while being measured against the wrong register. Corrected in props_realized above by re-mapping to the real register, and the re-mapping exposed the substantive gap.

4. generalize_use_cases — read. Claim: every story covered, extensions numbered off steps, no UI mechanics. Verified story-by-story (the mapping is in stories_generalized). Extensions all hang off a numbered step. Checked for UI mechanics by looking for tool names in scenario steps: none — the steps say 'the machine refuses'. HOLDS.

5. THE M1 FRAME — frame_delta-2 opened and read, not remembered. Confirms the corrected N2 pass line ('ONE call AND the result carries the caller's requested surrounding lines'), and confirms N10, N11, N12 were added by the rewalk. Then frame_delta-1, the SUPERSEDED first pass, was opened to recover the full N1-N9 register — which is itself the first live proof of N11's pass line: prior evidence survived a reopen and was readable when needed. That was not a rehearsal; I needed those needs and they were there.

A BLESS IS NOT PROOF, applied: gate_motivation passed earlier in this rewalk. I did not treat that as evidence for anything here; the frame's contents were re-read from disk.
payload.validate_round:
BUILT THE RIGHT THING — against the frame, the vision, and the need register rather than against my own plan.

WHAT IS MISSING (the finding):
- N3 'know the rules that bind this step' — guidance arriving resolved in the packet — has NO story and therefore no use case. It is squarely in scope (it is one of the three written-but-never-collected mechanisms that motivated the whole iteration) and I intend to build it. At M3 it would produce requirements that no scenario step supports — unsourced requirements, which is precisely what this gate exists to prevent.
- N8 'the record survives carelessness' — evidence outliving a deleted tag or a flagless push — has NO story. Its pass line is concrete and testable and nothing at M2 reaches it.
- N9 'the audit distinguishes computed from asserted' — NO story. S5 is adjacent but shows the LINT deciding; it never shows the owner telling a computed check from an asserted one, which is the entire need.

WHAT IS OUT OF SCOPE: nothing. I checked each use case against draw_context's binding excluded list. UC-G ext 3a touches the phone, which the excluded list rules out — but it does so by REFERENCING behaviour i8d already shipped, not by proposing work. That is citation, not scope creep. Allowed, and flagged here so the distinction is on the record rather than assumed.

WHAT IS WRONG: the props mislabelling in write_stories, described in the verify round. Corrected here; the underlying story content survives the correction.

ASKS NO CHECK COVERED — the drift indicator I was told to watch. Three of them, all from owner instructions issued after the frame was written: engine promotion as a real step (S3/UC-D), refusals rather than confident wrong answers (S4/UC-E), and identifiers expanded for a reader who cannot see them (S7/UC-G). These have stories and use cases but no NEED. The register is stale, not the stories. This direction of gap does not violate the gate's criterion — both props are realized — but leaving it unrecorded is how a design quietly drifts from its register, so it is recorded and M3 sources those requirements to the stories and the rulings.

AGAINST THE GOAL SYSTEM: G5 (a review happens because something asks for it) ranks first. This gate is the first in the project's history to be ASKED for these four rounds, and asking produced a finding that four gates of unaided diligence did not. That is direct evidence for G5's priority over G2, which is the exact ordering the vision claims.
payload.redteam_round:
THE OPPOSING CASE, argued before endorsing anything.

CASE FOR PASSING ANYWAY — steelmanned. The gate's own criterion is 'every value prop realized by at least one story'. Both props are realized. N3, N8 and N9 are NEEDS, not props, and the criterion does not mention needs. On a literal reading this gate passes cleanly, and reopening costs a cycle over a technicality that the M3 requirement register would catch anyway — because writing requirements is exactly where an unstoried need becomes visible. Reopening now is ceremony: it performs rigour for the record at real cost.

WHY THAT CASE LOSES, citing the rubric rather than an impression. The rubric is meth-gate-review's own framing: 'requirements written on unblessed stories propagate garbage', which is this gate's stated purpose — the user-level picture stops HERE for judgment before any system-level writing begins. A need with no story is a system-level requirement waiting to be written on nothing. Deferring it to M3 relocates the defect downstream and calls that a saving. It also loses on the owner's standing law: requirements are never weakened. Reading a criterion as narrowly as it can possibly be read, in order to pass, IS weakening it — and this iteration already contains one instance of exactly that move, where R3 (a match carries context) was 'satisfied' by a design that returned locations only and an ADR explaining why that was fine. That ADR is retired. I am not repeating the move two milestones later.

KILL-CRITERION for the REOPEN verdict — what would have to be true for reopening to be the wrong call: that the three gaps are cosmetic, i.e. that N3, N8 and N9 are already covered somewhere I did not look, OR that they are out of scope and should be struck from the register instead. I looked for both. Every story was re-read against the three needs: S5 touches N9's subject matter but never shows the distinguishing act; nothing anywhere reaches N8's pass line about a deleted tag; N3 appears in the vision's own indictment ('four laws minted this afternoon will never reach a packet') and in no scenario step. And all three are in scope by draw_context's boundary — guidance collection and record durability are both INSIDE. The kill-criterion is not met.

SECOND KILL-CRITERION, on the other side — what would make the reopen too WIDE: if closing the gaps required amending the M1 frame, the cone would swallow all of M2 and the cost would genuinely exceed the finding. It does not. The three needs are ALREADY IN the register; only the stories are missing. So the cone is two states, write_stories and generalize_use_cases, and this gate. Checked rather than assumed — the stale-register issue in the other direction is handled by recording it and sourcing at M3, not by reopening M1.

SCALED TO RISK: this is not a trivial gate. It is the last point at which the user-level picture is judged before requirements are written on it, and it is the first gate in this project ever to be asked for these rounds. Full scrutiny is proportionate.

HONEST WEAKNESS OF THIS ROUND, per the risk already logged about mandatory rounds degrading into ceremony: I am the author of the work I am red-teaming, and nothing here can fix that. What the round can do is bind form — name a kill-criterion and go look. I did, and it changed the verdict from pass to reopen, which is at least evidence that this instance was not decorative.
payload.verdict:
REOPEN.

STATES: write_stories, and its downstream cone (generalize_use_cases, and this gate).

REASON: three needs in the register — N3 (the rules that bind this step arrive resolved in the packet), N8 (the record survives carelessness), N9 (the audit distinguishes computed from asserted) — have no story and therefore no use case. This gate is the last point at which the user-level picture is judged before requirements are written on it; passing would send M3 to write requirements on nothing, which is the specific failure this gate exists to prevent.

SECOND, LESSER REASON: write_stories claims each slideshow realizes 'a named value prop' and names eight props that the frame does not contain. The re-fill states the two real props and maps each story to the needs it serves.

NOT REOPENED, and why: the M1 frame stands. Three stories (engine promotion, refusals, expanding identifiers) realize no numbered need, because the register predates the owner rulings that produced them. That is a stale register, not a wrong one, and it is handled by recording it here and sourcing those requirements to the stories and rulings at M3 — not by reopening M1 and re-walking all of M2 to add three needs.

NOT A SILENT PASS, and not an override: nothing here is blessed past an unmet criterion. The unmet part is going back.

WORTH SAYING PLAINLY: this is the first gate in this project's history to be handed the four rounds by its own evidence form, and it did not survive its own review. Four gates walked earlier today with the same author and the same diligence and no form asking — and all four passed.
